collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a teen aged 14-17; in the story (name1) has albinism, with very pale skin and white hair)

collection.description: A villager with albinism weaves fine sun hats, and a teen eyes the newest one: make the teen one, or teach them to weave.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has albinism: very pale skin, white hair, and eyes that don't like bright sun. On Isola, under that sun, that means hats. (subject.He/she) has been weaving them for years, and (subject.he/she) has become very, very good at it: wide brims, tight weave, little shells around the edge. (friend) has been eyeing (subject.his/her) newest one with naked envy.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) weaves (friend) a hat of (friend.his/her) own: not quite as wide, but just as fine. (friend) wears it everywhere. Within a month, half the teens in the village want one. (subject) now has a queue of customers outside (subject.his/her) hut. (subject.He/she) is pretending to be annoyed about it. (subject.He/she) is not annoyed about it at all.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) teaches (friend) to weave a hat. It takes days. (friend)'s first attempt is lopsided and lets in sun through several holes. (subject) wears it for a whole afternoon anyway, out of solidarity, and gets a sunburned spot on the top of (subject.his/her) head. (subject.He/she) shows it to (friend) without a word. (friend)'s second hat is much better.
